transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-10 16:00 PDT | Duration: 56 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Derek Alvarez (Redwood SE), Hannah Li (Redwood CSM); Tomás Rivera (Head of ML, Sunspire), Priya Singh (CTO), Emily Park (Security Lead), Raj Patel (Infra)
--- Auto-generated summary (may contain inaccuracies) ---
Quick notes: Sunspire piloting personalized recommendations; PII in training data; prefer private deployment but want cost comps; compliance gating for production.
--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. quick intros from our side, I'm Maya, AE for Redwood, i handle the commercial side.
[00:05] Derek Alvarez: hi all, Derek Alvarez, solutions engineer, i'll handle the technical deep dives and any benchmark questions.
[00:08] Hannah Li: hannah, customer success will own onboarding and runbooks, happy to coordinate.
[00:12] Priya Singh: priya here, cto at sunspire. we have a tight timeline, hoping to move to pilot in q3.
[00:16] Tomás Rivera: tomás, head of ml. we run recommendation models and some user PII in embeddings.
[00:19] Emily Park: emily, security lead. my focus is data residency, key management, and audit logs.
[00:22] Raj Patel: raj, infra. I'll be the liaison for on-prem and network.
[00:27] Maya Chen: great, objective today is to understand security requirements and hosting preferences so we can recommend Hosted, Dedicated or Private. feel free to interrupt.
[00:33] Priya Singh: sounds good. first big question: do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO-27001? and can we get the artifacts?
[00:38] Maya Chen: yes, we are SOC2 Type II and ISO-27001 certified. we'll send the attestation and the control matrix after the call, also a link to the security questionnaire — note that some redactions are standard.
[00:43] Emily Park: okay good. second, SSO: we require SAML-based SSO with SCIM provisioning and role mappings to our groups. what depth of RBAC do you provide?
[00:50] Derek Alvarez: we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based at the org, project, and token scopes; you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. there are some platform roles that are fixed but we can do custom role mappings for enterprise plans — for Private you get additional RBAC surface and audit hooks.
[00:58] Tomás Rivera: when you say token scopes, can we bind tokens to model access and rate limits per service? we need strict separation between staging and prod models.
[01:05] Derek Alvarez: yes, tokens can be scoped to specific models and routes, and you can set per-token quotas. for Dedicated, you also have tenant isolation in the GPU pools which helps.
[01:12] Emily Park: KMS — must be customer-managed keys. do you support rotating keys, HSM-based keys and do we keep control of encryption keys in Private?
[01:19] Maya Chen: short answer: yes. for Hosted we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) where we never persist plaintext. for Dedicated, you can attach your KMS as well, and Private gives you full control — HSM on prem or using your cloud HSM. Derek, anything to add re: key rotation?
[01:29] Derek Alvarez: rotation is supported, and we have documented key-change procedures. in Hosted there's a rekey flow that rotates envelope keys with zero-downtime for stored artifacts. for Private, it's entirely under your ops. i will share the runbook with specifics.
[01:37] Priya Singh: good. audit logs — how granular? we need admin-level logging, dataset access, inference requests, and model version rollouts in the logs. retention needs to be at least 1 year, possibly 3 for some regulated lines.
[01:45] Derek Alvarez: our audit logs include admin actions, API access (request metadata), model deploy events, and token issuance. retention defaults to 90 days on Hosted but can be extended for Dedicated/Private; enterprise add-on for extended retention to 3+ years. logs can be pushed to your SIEM (syslog, S3, or cloud logging).
[01:56] Emily Park: is there a tamper-evident mechanism? chain-of-custody?
[02:00] Derek Alvarez: logs are signed and there's an append-only store for critical events in Dedicated/Private. for Hosted we provide integrity checks and can stream to your immutable storage for extra assurance. note: wording in our docs sometimes says "append backed" which is shorthand, i'll send the detailed spec.
[02:12] Tomás Rivera: data residency — we need EU-only processing for EU customers. can we guarantee region pinning?
[02:17] Maya Chen: region pinning is supported. Hosted API supports region selection for request routing. Dedicated gives you a capacity pool in a region, and Private obviously runs in your VPC or on-prem so residency is under your control.
[02:27] Raj Patel: on-prem — what's the deployment footprint? what GPUs, orchestration, networking? and approx lead time?
[02:33] Derek Alvarez: our on-prem package has two flavors: full private control plane + inference nodes, or control plane in your VPC with private inference nodes. typical footprint depends on model family — for 7B-13B models, a small cluster with 4x A100/80GB-ish equivalents. we'll give a sizing guide after we see your expected QPS. lead time: discovery to pilot can be 4-8 weeks depending on SRE windows and hardware procurement.
[02:46] Priya Singh: procurement is tight, we may need to go Dedicated first then migrate to Private. cost question: what's the delta between Dedicated and Private? rough numbers suffice now.
[02:54] Derek Alvarez: rough thumb rule: Dedicated is lower management overhead and shorter lead time, unit costs slightly higher than Private if you run at sustained peak. Private has higher upfront ops but can be cost advantageous at scale, especially with spot-like capacity. i'll pull numbers and a TCO sheet.
[03:08] Maya Chen: also note smart routing and fallback: with Dedicated you can set policies to fall back to a lower-cost hosted variant if capacity spikes. that often helps with cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:16] Emily Park: encryption in transit — do you use mTLS for internal service traffic and TLS for external? any client cert requirements for private endpoints?
[03:22] Derek Alvarez: all external endpoints use TLS 1.2/1.3, mutual TLS is available for Private and Dedicated if you want client certs. internal service-to-service uses mTLS in our control planes.
[03:31] Tomás Rivera: operational question: how do you handle KV cache or prefix caching? we store some user vectors and don't want them leaking across tenants.
[03:38] Derek Alvarez: isolation is enforced at multiple layers: caching keys are namespaced per-tenant; Dedicated has hardware isolation pools; Private is fully isolated. caches can be encrypted at rest and purged on tenant termination.
[03:46] Priya Singh: SLA and availability — we need 99.95 for production inference paths. do you offer that on Dedicated?
[03:52] Maya Chen: yes, Dedicated has SLA options up to 99.95 with business continuity playbooks and burst capacity options; Private SLAs are part of the enterprise contract and depend on your ops. Hosted tier has best-effort for free tiers but higher SLAs on paid plans.
[04:06] Emily Park: curious about threat modeling — do you provide pen test results or allow third-party assessments?
[04:11] Maya Chen: we do annual third-party pen tests and provide summaries; customers can arrange contractual assessments on Private deployments. we'll include the pen-test executive summary in the packet.
[04:18] Tomás Rivera: latency targets — we need sub-100ms 1-token latency for the recommenders. is that realistic on Dedicated?
[04:24] Derek Alvarez: sub-100ms 1-token is aggressive but achievable for trimmed model configs and short context lengths on Dedicated with colocated GPUs and optimized kernels. we'll need to run a benchmark with your prompt shapes; can you share typical sequence lengths and RPS?
[04:34] Tomás Rivera: typical inference payloads are 80–120 tokens, bursty traffic up to 80 qps.
[04:39] Derek Alvarez: noted. that profile maps to a small Dedicated pool; i'll model latency curves. we'll probably suggest batching config and client-side streaming to meet targets.
[04:47] Priya Singh: SLAs aside, how do you handle data deletion requests — e.g., GDPR right to be forgotten — especially for cached embeddings?
[04:54] Maya Chen: we support object-level deletion and can run purge jobs for embeddings and caches. for Hosted we follow an API-assisted deletion flow; for Dedicated/Private you have deterministic deletion controls. we log deletion ops for audit.
[05:03] Emily Park: one more — licensing and export controls; any restrictions on model weights? we plan to use open models but have internal vetting.
[05:09] Derek Alvarez: most of the catalog is open models; for certain third-party licensed models there are export and redistrib clauses — we'll provide the model license matrix. you can also bring-your-own-models into Private.
[05:20] Priya Singh: this is helpful. what's the typical onboarding timeline to go from pilot to production?
[05:25] Hannah Li: for a standard pilot (8–12 weeks) then prod ramp another 4–8 weeks depending on compliance gates. Private may add lead time. we'll put a proposed timeline in the follow-up.
[05:33] Tomás Rivera: ok action items?
[05:36] Maya Chen: recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO certs and pen-test summary; Derek will produce TCO and sizing for Dedicated vs Private; Hannah will send onboarding checklist; Raj and Derek to schedule an on-prem scoping call week of 6/21. Emily to share retention policy and key rotation cadence.
[05:46] Priya Singh: perfect, we'll review docs and get procurement lined up.
[05:49] Emily Park: quick clarification: does Redwood retain any plaintext of customer data in Hosted?
[05:52] Derek Alvarez: no, we do not persist customer plaintext. tokens are processed in memory; any stored artifacts are encrypted with envelope keys; with customer-managed KMS we never have access to the unwrapped keys.
[06:02] Raj Patel: thanks everyone.
[06:04] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet by tomorrow.
[06:07] Priya Singh: thanks, talk soon.
--- End of transcript ---
